LEARNING PATH LESSON · SIGHT WORDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

And — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

Five minutes, one card: say “and” clearly, use it in a real sentence (“Cats and dogs play.”) and finish with one small game.

What it means

It joins two or more things together.

How to teach it

  1. Hold up the card and read “and” slowly, sliding a finger under it. Point out its shape: an a, an n and a d standing in a row, with a tall d to finish.
  2. Ask your child to find the first letter on the canvas and draw a ring around it, then say the whole word.
  3. Play the game below, say “and” one last time and stop while it is still fun.

How to say it

Say each sound clearly, a-n-d, and end with a light d. In fast talking it shrinks to un.

Where to use it

Say it in a real sentence: “Cats and dogs play.” Then try “I like red and blue.” Where to spot it: lists, such as bread and butter, mom and dad.

Try this game

Name two things you see, then link them with and: socks and shoes, up and down. Let your child add a third.

Understanding check

Tomorrow, show the card and say nothing. If your child reads “and” at once, it has arrived; if not, play the game again the day after.

Parent tips

Do not drill “and” on its own for long. Slip it into the books you read today and let the story do the practicing.

This lesson pairs with the And flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sight Words (Class 29).
